topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer treatments and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore standard therapeutic approaches such as surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that take advantage of cancer-specific vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted small-molecule inhibitors directed at hyperactive oncogenic kinases and detail the molecular mechanisms that lead to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered antibodies to directly target tumor surface receptors, mediate cytotoxicity, and deliver lethal chemical payloads to malignant cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell redirection strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and explore therapeutic strategies to activate and engineer T cells through checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overall clinical landscape of cancer treatment, including historical survival trends, barriers like tumor heterogeneity, and future directions in personalized care and trial design.
